classification.difficultyReason: Find the supplementary and remaining triangle angles, use the sine rule for a sight line, then resolve its vertical component, following the taught example.

content.prompt: To find the height of a mountaintop, a surveyor takes measurements from two accessible points $A$ and $B$ as shown below. Find the height $h$ of the mountain, correct to the nearest metre.

spec.description: Horizontal baseline A–B–C, vertical CD, sight lines AD and BD, and a right-angle mark at C. Decorative mountain silhouette and shading omitted.
spec.mathematics: AB = 321 m; angle DAC = 31 degrees; angle DBC = 47 degrees; CD = h. Coordinates derive the two sight-line angles exactly.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and the unknown h are visible.

answer.short:
$439\text{ m}$.

Use the sine rule in $\triangle ABD$, then $h=BD\sin47^\circ$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}
\angle ABD &= 180^\circ-47^\circ=133^\circ\\
\angle ADB &= 180^\circ-31^\circ-133^\circ=16^\circ
\end{align*}$$
By the sine rule in $\triangle ABD$,
$$\begin{align*}
\frac{BD}{\sin31^\circ} &= \frac{321}{\sin16^\circ}\\
BD &= \frac{321\sin31^\circ}{\sin16^\circ}.
\end{align*}$$
In right-angled $\triangle BCD$,
$$\begin{align*}
h &= BD\sin47^\circ\\
h &= \frac{321\sin31^\circ\sin47^\circ}{\sin16^\circ}\\
h &\approx 438.6658\text{ m}.
\end{align*}$$
The height of the mountain is $439\text{ m}$, to the nearest metre.
